audit.whatIsWrong: content win[2] and win[3] read Skill while whys[2] and whys[3] say your Q pattern plus Grievous Wounds out-trade his sustain and the stage stays yours. win[4] reads Warwick while whys[4] says Level 6 remains Aatrox's. win[5] reads Skill while whys[5] says first item swings extended fights to you.
audit.why: Warwick's sustain is health-gated — Eternal Hunger only heals below 50% and triples below 25% — so a full-health Warwick in an even trade heals nothing at all. The packet chart reads Warwick, Warwick, then Aatrox for every stage after. 49.51% over 1923 games.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-2 stay Warwick; Level 3 through Two+ items all read Aatrox.

audit.whatIsWrong: late calls Infinite Duress 'a low-cooldown suppression R' and gives no number, and no other ability carries a cooldown either.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 — a long cooldown, not a low one. Calling it low tells the player to fear it constantly instead of counting it and duelling the moment it is spent. Jaws of the Beast is 8s, Primal Howl 15s, Blood Hunt 80s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: 110s rank-1 R, 8s Q and 15s Primal Howl written into the spikes, mid and late; 'low-cooldown' removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is never mentioned anywhere in the entry, and it is the ability that breaks your combo. It gives him damage reduction for 2.5 seconds and then fears everyone nearby for a second, either when it expires or the moment he re-activates it. The entry also never states that Eternal Hunger's healing is gated on HIS health, not yours.
audit.why: Riot's text: Primal Howl — 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second'; Eternal Hunger — 'If Warwick is below 50% health, he heals the same amount. If Warwick is below 25% health, this healing triples.' The correct read is the opposite of the entry's: a healthy Warwick has no sustain, and the fight turns not when YOU are low but when HE drops under half. A fear landing mid-combo is what wastes your third swing.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl named with its 2.5s damage reduction and the fear on expiry or recast, in spikes[0] and mid; the below-50 and below-25 thresholds stated as his healing gate.

audit.why: Grievous Wounds is already named in four places, which is right — Eternal Hunger and Jaws of the Beast both heal. Worth adding that Jaws deals damage based on your MAXIMUM health, so stacking HP against him feeds the bite rather than answering it.
audit.corrected: Max-health scaling of Jaws of the Beast stated in the full-layer tldr.

edits.before: Your Q pattern out-trades his early sustain — land the third-Q knockup to interrupt his Q (Jaws of the Beast) channel and bring Grievous Wounds to cut his passive/W healing.
edits.after: Your Q pattern out-trades his sustain: Eternal Hunger heals nothing until he is below half health. Primal Howl (15s) fears you when it ends or on recast — that is what eats your third swing.

edits.before: You keep the edge through 6 but respect his R (Infinite Duress): it's a hard-CC suppression gap-close, so hold an E dash to reposition and bait it before you commit your combo; World Ender heal amp offsets his lifesteal.
edits.after: You keep the edge through 6, but Infinite Duress (110s) is a leap that suppresses the first champion it hits for 1.5s. Hold a dash to bait it — that is a long cooldown, so once it is gone the stage is entirely yours.

edits.before: Levels 3 onward tilt Aatrox and stay yours — your Q rotation plus Grievous Wounds out-trade his sustain, and the third-Q knockup interrupts his Q leap channel. The one thing to respect is his R at 6: Infinite Duress is a suppression that can lock your whole combo, so bait it with an E dash or trade knowing it's coming, then re-commit. At your first item you pull decisively ahead in extended brawls.
edits.after: Levels 3 onward stay yours — Eternal Hunger gives him nothing above 50% health, so an even trade is a losing one for him, and Grievous Wounds waits for the moment he drops. Primal Howl (15s) is the real interrupt: 2.5s of damage reduction, then a fear on expiry or on recast, so hold your knockup through it. At 6 bait the 110s Infinite Duress, then re-commit and finish.

edits.before: Warwick scales into a tanky, high-sustain diver with a reliable suppression ult, but once you're itemised your drain plus Grievous Wounds out-lasts his healing in a straight 1v1. Keep Grievous Wounds up, don't get caught alone under the HP threshold that supercharges his passive, and be ready for his R to flip a sloppy trade — otherwise the late-game duel is yours.
edits.after: Warwick scales into a tanky, high-sustain diver, but once you are itemised your drain plus Grievous Wounds out-lasts him in a straight 1v1. Blood Hunt marks you at half health and triples his bonuses under a quarter, so the real danger is being caught already low. Count the 110s Infinite Duress and duel him the moment it is spent — otherwise the late-game duel is yours.

edits.before: Sustain through trades with passive lifesteal and W
edits.after: Drop below half so Eternal Hunger starts healing

edits.before: Warwick changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Warwick Q, E fear, low-HP healing, and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Warwick wants to enter inside Aatrox clean Q hits on the outer edge (where it hurts most), force melee trades, and punish Aatrox after Q/E are down.
edits.after: Warwick changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Primal Howl (E, 15s), 2.5 seconds of damage reduction that ends in a fear, and an Eternal Hunger that heals nothing until Warwick himself falls below half health. Aatrox wins by spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, holding the knockup through the howl, and buying Grievous Wounds — Jaws of the Beast scales on maximum health, so stacking HP only feeds the bite.

edits.before: Warwick Q, E fear, low-HP healing, and R
edits.after: Primal Howl ends in a 1s fear on you

notes: packet suspectNames flags 'Land Infinite Duress' as a probable wrong name — FALSE POSITIVE, the matcher is tripping on the leading verb; the name is correct per Riot Data Dragon. Blood Hunt is described in the entry as a chase tool, which is close enough to Riot's text (move speed toward and attack speed against enemies below 50% health) and was left alone; its 80s rank-1 cooldown now appears in late.
